IX.}}</noinclude>promisse is this, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Gen. 18, 10.''}}* ''According to this time vvil I come: and Sara shal haue a sonne''. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=10}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Gen. 25, 21.''}}* And not only she, But {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ ''Al the epistle surely to the Romanes needeth interpretatiõ, and is on wrapped with so great obscurities that to vnderstãd it we neede the helpe of the Holy Ghost, who by the Apostle did dictat these same things: but especially this place. Howbeit nothĩg pleaseth vs but that which is Ecclesiastical, that is, the sense of the Church''.}}∷ Rebecca also conceiuing {{sup|‖}} of one copulation, of Isaac our father. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=11}}† For vvhen they vvere {{sup|‖}} not yet borne, nor had done any good or euil (that the purpose of God according to election might stand) {{verse|chapter=9|verse=12}}† not of vvorkes, but of the caller it vvas said to her: {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Gen. 25, 23.''}}* ''That the elder shal serue the yonger'', {{verse|chapter=9|verse=13}}† as it is vvritten: {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mal. 1, 2.''}}* ''Iacob I loued, but Esau I hated''.

{{verse|chapter=9|verse=14}}† VVhat shal vve say then? {{sup|‖}} Is there iniquitie vvith God? God forbid. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=15}}† For to Moyses he saith, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Exo. 33. 19.''}}* ''I vvil haue mercie on vvhom I haue mercie: and I vvil shevv mercie to vvhom I vvil shevv mercie''. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=16}}† Therfore it is {{sup|‖}} not of the vviller, nor the runner, but of God that sheweth mercie. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=17}}† For the Scripture saith to Pharao: {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Exo. 9, 16.''}}* ''That {{sup|‖}} to this very purpose haue I raised thee, that in thee I may shevv my povver: and that my name may be renowmed in the vvhole earth''. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=18}}† Therfore on vvhom he vvil, he hath mercie: and vvhom he vvil, he doth indurate.

{{verse|chapter=9|verse=19}}† Thou saiest therfore vnto me: VVhy doth he yet complaine? for vvho resisteth his vvil? {{verse|chapter=9|verse=20}}† O man, {{sup|‖}} vvho art thou that doest ansvver God? Doth the vvorke say to him that vvrought it: VVhy hast thou made me thus? {{verse|chapter=9|verse=21}}† Or hath not {{sup|‖}} the potter of clay, povver, of the same masse to make one vessel vnto honour, and an other vnto contumelie? {{verse|chapter=9|verse=22}}† And if God vvilling to shevv vvrath, and to make his might knovven, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ That God is not the cause of any mans reprobation or damnation, othervvise then for punishment of his sinnes, he sheweth by that he expecteth al mens amendement with great patience, and consequently that they haue also free wil.}}∷ susteined in much patience the vessels of vvrath {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''`apted, fitted''.}}`apte' to destruction, {{verse|chapter=9|verse=23}}† that he might shevv the riches of his glorie vpon the vessels of mercie vvhich he prepared vnto glorie.

{{verse|chapter=9|verse=24}}† VVhom also he hath called, vs, not only of the Ievves, but also of the Gentiles, {{verse|chapter=9|verse=25}}† as in Osee he saith, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Os. 2, 23.''}}* ''I wil call that which is not my people, my people: and her that vvas not beloued, beloued: and her that hath not obteined mercie, hauing obteined mercie''. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=26}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Os. 1, 10.''}}* ''And it shal be, in the place vvhere it vvas said to them, you are not my people: there they shal be called the sonnes of the liuing God''. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=27}}† And Esaie crieth for Israel, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Esa. 10, 22.''}}* ''If the number of the children of Israel be as the sand of the sea, the remaines shal be saued''. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=28}}† ''For, consummating a word, and abbridging it in equitie: because a vvord abbridged shal our Lord make vpon the earth''. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=29}}† And as Esay foretold, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Esa. 1, 9.''}}* ''Vnles the Lord of Sabaoth had left vs seede: vve had been made like Sodom, and vve had been like as Gomorrha''.

{{verse|chapter=9|verse=30}}† What shal vve say then? That the Gentiles vvhich pursued not after iustice, haue apprehended iustice, but the iustice that is of faith. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=31}}† But Israel in pursuing the lavv of iustice, is not come vnto the lavv of iustice. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=32}}† VVhy so?<noinclude>{{rh|||Because}}</noinclude>
